newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate remains weak in flush market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate remains weak in flush market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 5.80 percent on Thursday as the market remained flush, dealers said.
They said many local and foreign banks were highly liquid, which had pressured all interbank rates downward.
Dealers said the market did not show any sign of funds leaving the system despite a widely expected Bank Negara lending maturity, said to be for two billion ringgit, on Thursday.
Such a maturity should push rates higher, they said.
"Now I doubt whether there actually is a maturity. Rates are still coming off which shows that there's no outflow," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "The money could already be in the system."
"There's so much liquidity in the market and if not for central bank support, the overnight would have gone lower," said another dealer.
There has been speculation that Bank Negara, through its agent banks, has been supporting the overnight from falling below its perceived floor of 5.80 percent.
Earlier, one-month money was at 7.35/40 percent against 7.40 percent on Wednesday, and three-month at 7.50 percent against 7.55.
One-week money was steady at 6.60/70 percent.

Market liquidity had improved significantly from the tightness seen in May, following recent lending by the central bank and maturity of Bank Negara bills worth a total two billion ringgit over the past week which were not rolled over.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher across the board on the softening of interbank rates in the cash market.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up 10 points to 92.66, or an implied yield of 7.34 percent.
The December contract also rose 10 to 92.77, or 7.23 percent and March 1998 was up eight to 92.82, or 7.18 percent.
